title: Visit to Drew's house and his needle-and-Teflon setup; wife Janessa links the forces

tellings.quote: So, we go to Drew's house. I take my wife and we spent, you know, four or five hours looking at his setup, looking what he's doing.

plain: In 2016, a NASA engineer named Charles Buhler says he and his wife Janessa spent four or five hours at the Florida home of an inventor named Andrew Arjima, known as Drew, studying a setup Drew had built from a needle and Teflon. Buhler says his wife was the one who saw the link between the forces at work. He tells it as something he saw himself, and he presents it as part of the road to what he calls antigravity propulsion, a way to move without pushing against anything.
